module_title: Mechanics I - Relative Motion, Constraints & Variable Mass
introduction: This advanced level explores complex mechanics primarily targeted at JEE Advanced and high-tier NEET questions. It involves shifting reference frames, dealing with accelerating observers, and handling systems where masses are constrained or changing.

core_concepts.title: Relative Velocity in 2D
core_concepts.description: Analyzes the motion of one body from the perspective of another moving body (V_AB = V_A - V_B). Classic applications include Rain-Man problems and River-Boat crossings.

core_concepts.title: Pseudo Force (Non-Inertial Frames)
core_concepts.description: When observing from an accelerating frame (like a decelerating car or an elevator accelerating upwards), you must apply an imaginary 'Pseudo Force' (F_p = -m * a_frame) to the object to make Newton's laws valid.

core_concepts.title: Constraint Relations
core_concepts.description: Mathematical relationships tying the velocities or accelerations of multiple bodies together. Common types include string constraints (length of string remains constant) and wedge constraints (bodies remain in contact).

core_concepts.title: Variable Mass Systems
core_concepts.description: Systems where mass changes over time (e.g., a rocket burning fuel). Newton's Second Law must be used in its pure momentum form: F = dp/dt = m(dv/dt) + v(dm/dt).

core_concepts.title: Spring Force (Hooke's Law)
core_concepts.description: The restoring force of an ideal spring is proportional to its extension/compression: F = -kx. When springs are cut, the tension changes instantaneously, unlike strings.

important_entities.name: Thrust Force
important_entities.significance: The forward push a rocket receives due to the backward ejection of exhaust gases at a relative velocity (v_rel).

important_entities.name: Virtual Work Method
important_entities.key_fact: Sum of Work done by Internal Tension is Zero.
important_entities.significance: The most powerful trick to solve complex pulley constraint relations. Σ T.x = 0 implies Σ T.v = 0 and Σ T.a = 0.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Shortest Path vs. Shortest Time (River Boat)
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: To cross a river in the shortest time, always aim straight across (perpendicular to flow). To take the shortest path (straight line across), you must swim upstream at an angle to cancel the river's flow velocity.

Pseudo force is always applied opposite to the direction of the frame's acceleration, regardless of the frame's velocity. A car braking (moving right, accelerating left) means the pseudo force on the passenger is to the right.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To find which way to hold the umbrella, simply reverse the velocity vector of the man and add it to the velocity vector of the rain.

exam_strategy_tips: For JEE Advanced, if a problem involves wedges moving while blocks slide on them, immediately switch to the reference frame of the moving wedge and apply pseudo force.
Practice writing equations for string constraints using the Virtual Work (Tension Trick) method to save massive amounts of time compared to standard geometry.
